newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Bancorex bank again raises interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Romania Bancorex bank again raises interest rates.

text.p: State-owned Romanian bank Bancorex said on Friday it would jack up interest rates again next week to protect depositors in response to tougher monetary policies aimed at slowing racing inflation.
The bank's sight rates will rise to an annual 40 percent, from next Monday, up from a previous 22 percent, Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA said in a statement.
Its one-month rate will rise by 20 points to 85 percent, while three-month and six-month deposits will pay an annual 80 percent, against a previous 65 and 67 percent respectively.
Bancorex's one-year rate will also go up by 13 points to 80 percent.

Earlier this year the bank raised its deposit rates after the central bank started to tighten monetary policies, which triggered an upswing in the one-week refinancing rate to 125.45 percent this week from a previous 90 percent.
On Thursday, another large state bank, Banca Comerciala Romana SA, said it would raise its deposit rates next week.

Romania's year-on-year inflation quickened to 56.9 percent last year from 27.8 percent in 1995 and is forecasted to jump to 97 percent this year, led by January's fuel price rise and planned liberalisation of electicity and food prices.
